1.explanation:
1. core/gather/gatherers/global-listeners.js only calls DOMDebugger.getEventListeners on the default execution context’s window, so any unload listeners registered in isolated (extension) contexts are never collected.
2. core/audits/no-unload-listeners.js simply consumes the GlobalListeners artifact and assumes it’s exhaustive; it therefore reports no unload handlers when an extension listener lives in a different context.
3. core/gather/driver/execution-context.js provides the machinery to evaluate in isolated worlds (via useIsolation), but GlobalListeners never leverages it. To fix this bug, GlobalListeners must iterate through all available execution contexts—default and isolated—using the ExecutionContext helper, aggregate unload listeners from each, and then feed those into the audit so that no-unload-listeners will correctly detect extension-injected handlers.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse against a page with the LastPass extension installed, the back/forward-cache audit (bf-cache) fails with “The page has an unload handler in the main frame,” yet the “Avoids unload event listeners” audit passes and reports zero unload listeners. Inspection in DevTools shows no unload listeners in the default world because LastPass registers its listener in an isolated content-script context, which the no-unload-listeners audit doesn’t inspect. This mismatch makes the root cause invisible to developers.
